steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Persuasive writing aims to convince the reader to agree with your viewpoint or take a specific action. It uses a range of techniques to appeal to logic, emotion, and credibility.

steps.title: Key idea 2
steps.body: Introduction: Hook the reader with a striking opening State your viewpoint clearly Outline what you'll discuss

steps.title: Key idea 3
steps.body: Main Body: Present your strongest argument first Support each point with evidence Use a new paragraph for each point Address counter-arguments

steps.title: Key idea 4
steps.body: Conclusion: Summarise your main points Reinforce your viewpoint End with a powerful call to action

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Name three persuasive techniques and explain how each works. | Why is it important to address counter-arguments in persuasive writing? | Write an opening paragraph persuading your school to introduce a healthy eating policy.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Rhetorical questions (make reader think), emotive language (evoke feelings), statistics (add credibility) - plus many other valid techniques. | It shows you've considered different viewpoints and strengthens your argument by preemptively refuting opposition. | Your paragraph should include: clear viewpoint, rhetorical question or hook, and persuasive techniques.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always establish your viewpoint in the first paragraph Use a range of techniques - don't repeat the same one Support every point with evidence or examples Address the counter-argument to show balanced thinking End with a powerful, memorable call to action Use paragraphs to structure your argument clearly Check your spelling and punctuation carefully
